$comment: Schema for /qa-test's summary.json (reports/tickets/{SPRINT}/<ticket-key>/summary.json). The ONLY narrative-adjacent artifact /qa-test persists (per .claude/rules/reports.md §1) — it must carry every field a later consumer needs: 1b's cross-sprint duplicate check reads `date`; 5e's Feature Release Gate reads `regression`; 5g records `promotion`; `layer` is derived at 1b item 2b and `release` resolved at 5e.0, both persisted at 5e.3, and their only reader is /ba-analyze docs release. Replace <..> placeholders; 0/[]/null are empty defaults.

timing.$comment: Wall-clock for THIS /qa-test run. Per-suite durations are a different record and already live in reports/regression/history.json (durationField() in scripts/lib/regression-triage.ts derives them from the runner envelope) — do not duplicate them here. This block exists because the 40-minute regression window and the FAST/FULL split are both claims about cost, and before it the schema carried 78 keys and not one duration, so neither claim could be checked. regression_predicted_minutes is the makespan `regression:select --target` predicted; regression_actual_minutes is what the run took. An order-of-magnitude gap between them is the known ×18-×88 estimatedMinutes defect surfacing (see scripts/lib/suite-selection.ts) — record it, don't reconcile it away.

build.$comment: THREE version facts, not one, because they answer different questions and disagreeing on them produces the two worst QA outcomes available: filing a bug against a feature that was never deployed, and signing off a fix that never landed. `platform`/`theme`/`relevant_modules` are the DECLARED state (vc-deploy-dev backend/packages.json — git). `deployed` is what GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/modules actually reports — the ground truth, and routinely different (deploy in flight, failed, partially applied). A failed probe records the string UNKNOWN and NEVER falls back to declared. Full precedence rule: .claude/templates/agent-dispatch.md § Build Verification.

deployed.$comment: Probed, not read from git. UNKNOWN is a legal value; an absent/guessed value is not.

releasedThrough.$comment: Written by 1b item 2a from .claude/knowledge/domain/release-ledger.md. `ledger_generated` is that file's own `generated:` date — the run's freshness bound (stale after 45 days). `behind[]` lists components where deployed < released, i.e. shipped upstream but not testable here: those are NOT_DEPLOYED, never FAIL. `breaking[]` lists ⚠ BREAKING rows in the component(s) under test — a non-empty array is a FAST->FULL forcing condition (see 1b item 2a), so recording it is what makes that routing decision re-derivable afterwards. Empty arrays are the normal, correct state on a quiet month; null means the ledger was not consulted, which is a gap, not a zero.

release.$comment: Resolved at 5e.0 and written at 5e.3, for a PASS/PASS_WITH_NOTES verdict (5f only POINTS at /ba-analyze; it computes nothing) — the MACHINE half of the per-ticket release-note fragment. The prose half is ba-doc-writer's reports/ba/release-notes/<ticket>-<layer>-release-note.md, and this block is the ONLY thing that doc may take a layer, a version or a breaking flag from (ba-doc-writer never re-derives them; a second derivation site is how the two drift). It exists because the top-level `layer` is the axis a release note routes on (layer -> audience -> skeleton, .claude/knowledge/ba/virto-doc-style.md §9) and nothing here recorded it: `regression.suites` carries the layer of what was RE-TESTED, `build` carries versions of what was DEPLOYED, and neither answers 'which surface did THIS ticket change'. A null block means the release step never ran (FAIL/BLOCKED, or a run predating the block) — a gap, not 'nothing shipped'. `fragment` null WITH a non-null `refusal` is the opposite: the step ran and declined, and the reason is the finding. `component_versions`/`platform_version` are copied from build.deployed (PROBED) — never from build.relevant_modules (declared git state) and never from release-ledger.md, which records what shipped UPSTREAM, not what is deployed here; UNKNOWN is legal, an absent or guessed version refuses the fragment. `breaking` is true only from build.releasedThrough.breaking[] or a cited contract change in the diff — never from ticket, PR or commit prose, so breaking:true with breaking_source:null is a defect in the fragment.

documentation.$comment: Written at 5h, AFTER the 5f transition — the record of the ordinary product DOCUMENTATION published for this ticket (§10 of .claude/knowledge/ba/virto-doc-style.md), which is a different artifact from the `release` block above: that one is a what-shipped record, this one is how-do-I-use-this. Deliberately carries NO version fields — a how-to does not quote a build number, which is why `no-version` is absent from this block's refusal set. `audiences` is derived from the top-level `layer` via the §9.1 row and may hold MORE than one entry (the layer's audience is a floor, not a ceiling — the ordinary §1 rule, unlike the release note's one-per-layer inversion); `sales` is never among them. `files` are the reports/ba/<ticket>-<slug>-<audience>-guide.md paths, and `amended` names any pre-existing guide updated in place rather than forked. `comment_posted` is FALSE when the guides were written but the operator declined the tracker post — distinct from `published:false`, which means nothing was written at all. A null block means 5h never ran (a gap); `published:false` WITH a non-null `refusal` is the opposite — the step ran and declined, and the reason is the finding.

status_transitions.$comment: Every status hop this run made, AND every hop it skipped, with the reason. Single source of truth for the rules: .claude/knowledge/execution/ticket-status-transitions.md. WHY IT EXISTS: a skipped transition previously left NO trace in any artifact, so "the ticket was never moved" and "the ticket was moved and the note was lost" were indistinguishable after the fact — and the 5f table had two rows for a four-value verdict vocabulary, so a BLOCKED run silently left the ticket parked in in-testing. A run makes at most TWO hops: the opening hop at 1a, the moment the feature-test route resolves (never confirmed, reversible, and on Jira the precondition both closing transitions need; it moved here from Step 4 because in-testing means QA OWNS the ticket, which is true when the run is accepted rather than when the first browser opens — at Step 4 the ticket read as unclaimed through 30+ minutes of context, modelling, authoring and seeding) and the closing hop at 5f (always confirmed, terminal for the run). qa-lead is the only actor: no specialist, runner, verifier, doer or sub-agent transitions a ticket. NULL for this whole field means no hop was even attempted, which is a gap and not a clean run (the axes.md §2 rule one level down); an EMPTY ARRAY means the run reached the tracker and deliberately made no move. On --iterate the closing hop appears ONCE, at loop exit, whatever the round count.

status_transitions.skipped: verdict BLOCKED — blocker comment posted, ticket stays in-testing awaiting a re-run

epic.$comment: parent = the Epic this story belongs to (null if none). roll_up is written only on an --epic serial run (in the Epic's own summary), combining the child-story verdicts + the cross-story E2E into one Epic recommendation.

ac_dod_estimate.$comment: Filled by 5b. ac_coverage_pct = conditions_with_evidence/conditions_total. dod_* are null/0 when the ticket states no DoD (1e DoD field = 'none stated').

iterations.$comment: Only when invoked with --iterate (Step 5k — .claude/skills/qa-test/modes.md). `rounds` = how many test(->fix->re-test) rounds ran (the initial run IS round 1); `outcome` = how the loop ended. `per_round` is the record 5k step 4 demands in prose — 'a per-round summary (what each round fixed, what still fails)' — and previously had nowhere to live: every other field in this file is single-valued, so round 2 overwrote round 1's verdict, counts, regression run_id and timing, and the cap-reached hand-off cited per-round numbers no artifact could support. INVARIANT: per_round.length === rounds and per_round[i].round === i+1. WRITTEN AT THE END OF EVERY ROUND, not at loop exit — the loop can STOP at any round (G0 BAIL, BLOCKED, the cap, a dropped session), and a history persisted only on a clean exit is missing exactly when it is needed. `enabled: true` with an empty per_round is a contradiction, not a default: it means the run claimed the loop and recorded no round.

per_round.$comment: One entry per round. WHAT THE SINGLE-VALUED TOP-LEVEL FIELDS MEAN ONCE THERE ARE N ROUNDS: `verdict`, `total_cases`/`passed`/`failed`/`blocked`, `regression.*`, `regression_triage.*` and `promotion` are the LATEST round's — the build a human is being asked to ship — NOT the best and NOT the first. `bugs_filed`, `bugs_not_filed` and `new_cases_authored` are CUMULATIVE across rounds (a round-1 Sub-task must not vanish from the artifact because round 2 filed nothing). `timing` is the WHOLE run: started_at = round 1's start, finished_at = the last round's finish, steps.step4/steps.step5 summed across rounds. Round 1's own numbers survive ONLY here — never reconstruct them from the top level.

build.$comment: What this round ACTUALLY tested, probed from GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/modules — never assumed from the deploy PR, because /qa-deploy-pr --verify is advisory by its own contract. The loop's whole claim is that the code changed between rounds; unprobed, a 'still failing' round is indistinguishable from a deploy that never landed. UNKNOWN is legal; a guess is not. `deploy_pr` is the /qa-deploy-pr deploy PR (round >=2 only; null on round 1). `deploy_confirmed` records the mandatory human confirm before that deploy — false on round 1, and false at round >=2 means the loop deployed without asking, which is a defect in the run.

red_green.$comment: The re-run of exactly the previously-FAILED cases, as its OWN /qa-regression run (--ids), kept out of the C2 run so its pass rate answers one question and the release gate's >=80% floor keeps answering another (the floor came down from 95% on 2026-09-02; skills/qa-metrics/quality-gates.md owns it). Round 1: all null/empty — there is no previously-failed set yet, and that is not a gap. FAST: run_id stays null and `checklist_items` carries the re-run items instead of `cases`, because a FAST round re-runs failed checklist items through one agent and produces no RUN_ID.

regression.$comment: This round's change-scoped Artifact-C run, RE-SCOPED to the fix's diff (regression:select --repo <name> --diff <fix-PR range>), never reused from round 1 — round 1's scope came from the ticket's diff and cannot know what the fix touched. A non-null skipped_reason means the gate cannot be evaluated on this round.

bugs_carried.$comment: A bug THIS RUN filed in an earlier round that is still failing. Neither re-filed nor relabelled PRE-EXISTING: it keeps its original IN-SCOPE provenance and severity (so it still fails 5c this round) and gets one comment on its existing Sub-task. Re-filing would produce N tickets for one defect; PRE-EXISTING would stop it failing the ticket that caused it.

bugs_fixed.$comment: A bug filed in an earlier round whose case(s) went GREEN in this round. Commented on its own Sub-task and recorded here, deliberately NOT transitioned: TESTED is the furthest /qa-test may move anything and Done/Cancelled are forbidden, and the fix is an UNMERGED prerelease, so nothing has shipped. The human who merges closes it.

qa_fix.$comment: One /qa-fix invocation per in-scope fixable bug this round. outcome pr-open = G0-G7 cleared and a PR is open (never merged); bail = a G0 BAIL, which STOPs the loop and hands THAT bug to a human. An empty array on a FAIL round means no in-scope fixable bug remained and the loop fell back to the pointer close-out — a legitimate ending, and one the loop-level `outcome` alone cannot express.

artifacts.$comment: What this round changed in the durable artifacts, so a diff is attributable to a round rather than to 'the run'. `model_amendment` = a `## Round N` section appended to the ONE Step-1e model file (never a second dated file — a same-day round 2 collides on <TICKET>-<date>.md, and two files split one fault model in two). `cases_authored` = cases authored FROM a loop-confirmed defect, the strongest `plausible:` ground the KEEP gate accepts; they must be authored BEFORE the round that re-runs them or they execute nowhere and 5g holds them at Draft with PR-002. `checklist_section` names the appended section — the checklist is append-only because the RED->GREEN transition is the loop's deliverable.

still_failing: <one line per condition/case still red at the end of this round>

promotion.$comment: Filled by 5g (runs last, non-blocking). Cases are appended to regression/suites/ as Draft in Step 3; after Step 4 has executed them 5g flips each promotable case Draft→Automated via `npm run tc:promote:apply` (bare `tc:promote` is the DRY RUN and writes nothing), reverts non-promotable rows, and leaves a case that failed on a real in-scope bug at Draft with a reason. IT WRITES `Automated` ONLY, and only onto a row that is exactly `Draft` (scripts/test-cases/promote-cases.ts never touches any other status). `Reviewed`/`Manual` is a HUMAN call that 5g never makes — the `reviewed` array below records such a decision, it does not record something 5g did.

blocked.reason: unresolved {HYPOTHESIS} — <what stayed unknown> | failed on in-scope bug <link>

regression.$comment: TWO runs answering two different questions — C1 gates the VERDICT, C2 gates the RELEASE, and they must stay separate numbers. Fusing them is what put a ~40-minute suite sweep on the critical path to a verdict whose own criteria (atomic conditions, reconciled ACs, DoD items, BL-*, IN-SCOPE bugs) are every one of them a claim about THIS ticket, while a Critical FAIL in a neighbouring suite is PRE-EXISTING or OUT-OF-SCOPE by 5a's own provenance rules and fails nothing. A null run_id with a null skipped_reason is a GAP, not a clean run. On an --iterate run these are the FINAL round's; earlier rounds are in iterations.per_round[].regression.

c1.$comment: Step 4, on the verdict path. The exact set: this run's new Draft case IDs + every Step-2a RE-BASE case id, as /qa-regression <suites> --ids <IDs>. --ids IS the selection and is mutually exclusive with --cases/--also-ids; it reads no Priority at all, so an unreadable one is not a finding on this path. Its pass rate is the one 5b reconciles against. SKIPPED when the run authored no cases and disposed no RE-BASE — state it, because an omitted regression track reads exactly like a passing one.

c2.$comment: 5r — launched the instant 5c is RECORDED (5e is what publishes), overlapped with 5d and drafting 5e. regression:select --target 40 for the suites, then --cases critical; NO --also-ids, because this run's own cases have C1. THE FEATURE RELEASE GATE'S >=80% FLOOR IS DEFINED ON THIS run_id — not on c1, and not on whole-history. An IN-SCOPE finding here amends the recorded verdict ONCE, via 5c's existing table and with no new criteria. scope_exclusions names every suite that contributed zero Critical cases, because such a suite and a passing suite are otherwise indistinguishable. predicted and actual minutes are both recorded: the cost model is documented as wrong by x18-x88 for runner-native suites, so the prediction is a hint, and only the pair makes regression:recalibrate possible.

regression_triage.$comment: Filled by 5a item 0 for the C1 run, and AGAIN at 5r for the C2 run — /qa-triage-results <run_id> --fix, one invocation per RUN_ID, same taxonomy both times. run_ids[] carries both in execution order, and a C2 entry appearing here is what records that 5r triaged rather than merely ran. The three arrays mirror its triage-report.md tables (confirmed bugs / test-case fixes applied / dismissed) and are CUMULATIVE across both runs.

bugs_filed.$comment: One entry per confirmed bug filed at 5d. `severity` is recorded so the 5d severity floor is auditable from this artifact rather than only from the comment. On an --iterate run this array is CUMULATIVE across rounds; the round that filed each entry is in iterations.per_round[].bugs_filed.

bugs_not_filed.$comment: One entry per confirmed real bug held BELOW the 5d severity floor (Low/P3). Present and empty when there are none — an absent array is indistinguishable from a run that found none. `report` is the durable record; the floor drops a finding from the tracker, never from the run.

discovery.$comment: Step 3x, the discovery lane (FULL path only). NULL means the lane NEVER RAN; ran:false with a reason means it was skipped; an empty findings array means it ran and found nothing — three different facts that an absent block would collapse into one. It runs concurrently with 3a (test-data is browserless, so its one chrome/edge lane is free concurrency, never firefox) in a hard 25-minute box, and CLOSES BEFORE Artifact A, because all four of its outputs are inputs to authoring. It invokes /qa-exploratory ticket <key>, which owns the session; this pipeline owns only the charter. charter_sources records each of the five derived sources as covered or NOT_REACHED with a reason — an omitted source reads as a source with nothing in it. hypotheses_grounded and scenarios_new are kept APART on the same logic that splits visual.invariant_failures from visual.advisory: the first says the lane improved THIS run's cases, the second that it improved the corpus, and the first is the reason the lane runs before authoring rather than after. The lane FILES NO BUGS — they enter 5a's triage like any other finding. Spec: .claude/skills/qa-test/exploratory-lane.md

scenarios_new.$comment: fate PROMOTE means authored IN THIS RUN (a case id here), not deferred to a later sprint. oracle_ref NONE is a valid and valuable answer — it routes the row to the Oracle Feedback table.

visual.$comment: The design + accessibility axis. `surface` is derived at 1b item 2c beside `layer` (same discipline: derived, never asked, never defaulted) and decides whether the Step-4 visual lane dispatches at all; "unresolved" is treated as true, the one place this axis fails OPEN, because a wrongly-skipped visual pass leaves no trace anywhere while a wrongly-run one costs one agent. A NULL block means the step never ran — a gap, not a clean result; `ran:false` WITH a `skipped_reason` is the opposite, the step ran and declined. THE TWO ARRAYS ARE THE POINT: `invariant_failures[]` (BL-A11Y-*/BL-UI-*, all P1 for the a11y set) are ordinary findings — triaged at 5a, graded, filed under the 5d floor, able to fail 5c — while `advisory[]` (vs. DESIGN DRIFT/MISSING/UNSPEC/KNOWN_DIVERGENCE) is reported and NEVER fails the ticket. Keeping them apart is what makes the blocking rule auditable from this artifact instead of only from prose. Per-axis `verdict` null WITH a `skipped_reason` is legal and common — the design_spec axis needs /design-login, unavailable in web sessions and CI, and axe can be blocked by CSP; NEITHER may ever be recorded as a pass. Spec: .claude/skills/qa-test/visual-axis.md. Deliberately NOT owned here: BL-UI-001..005 layout stability, which keeps its existing owner (authoring tags + suite 048c).

a11y.$comment: WCAG 2.2 AA + BL-A11Y-001..004. Five of the six WCAG 2.2 additions (2.4.11/2.5.7/3.2.6/3.3.7/3.3.8) are manual-only and a clean axe run says nothing about them; screen-reader output cannot be verified at all. Scope is the gated themes (Coffee + Red).

design_system.$comment: Live resolved custom properties vs the generated token set (tokens:sync), no hardcoded literals, sized-control token + aspect equality.

design_spec.$comment: vs. DESIGN against DESIGN_SYSTEM_PROJECT_ID via DesignSync. `unresolved` > 0 downgrades an otherwise-clean axis to WARN and must be printed — a guessed expectation fails every correct implementation.

a11y_findings.$comment: BL-A11Y-* FAILs on a functional/feature/E2E ticket. These are FOUND, EVIDENCED and FILED as their own standalone ticket at their REAL severity — and they do NOT fail 5c. Accessibility is a cross-cutting property of a surface, not an acceptance criterion of the story that touched it, and the defect is usually pre-existing on the component. Kept in a SEPARATE array from invariant_failures[] for the same reason advisory[] is separate: it makes the blocking rule auditable from the artifact instead of only from prose. CARVE-OUT: when the ticket is ABOUT accessibility (a11y/WCAG remediation, ACs naming an accessibility outcome, a /qa-accessibility run) the finding blocks normally and belongs in invariant_failures[] instead. Spec: .claude/skills/qa-test/triage.md 7a

invariant_failures.$comment: May fail the ticket. `bug` is the 5d tracker key, or null when held below the severity floor (the reports/bugs/open/<severity>/ draft still exists and is named in bugs_not_filed).

advisory.$comment: NEVER fails the ticket. AMBIGUOUS is the one that needs a human: the spec contradicts an invariant or a WCAG criterion, and it is escalated in the 5e report rather than resolved by obeying the spec.

contract.$comment: The API contract-refresh axis. `surface` is derived at 1b item 2d beside `layer` (2b) and `visual.surface` (2c), same discipline: derived, never asked, never defaulted, "unresolved" treated as true — the axis fails OPEN because a skipped refresh leaves the run reading a snapshot of unknown age while a needless one costs one introspection call. A NULL block means the step never ran (a gap, not a clean refresh); surface:false WITH sources is the opposite — it ran and correctly declined. TWO ARTIFACTS, TWO COMMANDS, and neither freshens the other: `schema` is .claude/knowledge/api/graphql-schema.md (npm run schema:refresh — what 1c/1d/1e and the Step-3b authoring pack READ), `fixtures` is scripts/.graphql-schema.cache.json + the 74 test-data/graphql documents (npm run graphql:fixtures:validate:refresh — the gate, exits non-zero on drift). `schema.refreshed` takes the string UNKNOWN on an unreachable endpoint and NEVER falls back to the committed snapshot's own date (same rule as build.deployed); UNKNOWN downgrades every {DOC} GraphQL oracle to {HYPOTHESIS}. `fixtures.drift_in_scope[]` is the consequential array: an op the TICKET'S OWN DIFF touches is a 1e finding (a moved contract is a chain link and a candidate reverse edge), while `drift_out_of_scope[]` is recorded and not chased (cross-check build.releasedThrough.breaking[]). Neither array files a bug from the gate alone — a schema-validation failure is a claim about a query document, not about product behaviour. npm run schema:check is a liveness check, NOT a drift gate. Spec: .claude/skills/qa-test/contract-refresh.md

drift_in_scope.$comment: An op the ticket's own diff touches — a 1e Test Model input, and the OLD shape belongs in the regression scope. Fix the fixture via npm run graphql:fixtures:update.
drift_in_scope.model_ref: <scenario # or link in the Test Model>

drift_out_of_scope.$comment: Pre-existing drift or an unannounced upstream break. Recorded, named in the Step-5 report, NOT chased — fixing it is /qa-test-lifecycle's.

coverage_triage.$comment: Triage of the EXISTING cases this change invalidates, run at Step 2a on BOTH paths. `surface` is derived at 1b item 2e beside layer (2b), visual.surface (2c) and contract.surface (2d) — derived, never asked, never defaulted, "unresolved" treated as true, because a skipped triage leaves stale assertions nobody looks at again while a needless one costs one script run. A NULL block means the step never ran (a gap, not a clean triage); surface:false WITH sources is the opposite. WHY THE STEP EXISTS: the pipeline only ever asked what the corpus already COVERS, so a stale row was reachable only by FAILING at Step 4 and being triaged at 5a — and three things stop that firing (regression:select maps changed PATHS and misses a suite whose domain the path does not spell, while reporting unmappedPaths:[] because the fail-open widening needs a total vocabulary miss; --cases critical then drops the High rows; and a row that never runs is never triaged). Measured on VCST-5733: 62 existing assertions on a widget label PR#2444 renames, 45 of the 81 at-risk rows FILTERED_OUT of the run. DISPOSITIONS are a closed set and every hit takes exactly one: CONFIRMED (still correct) · REPAIR (mechanically stale — renamed selector/moved route/removed arg/dead @td() alias — fixed BEFORE the run via /qa-review-tests file <suite> --fix, safe precisely because it moves the mechanics and not the oracle, and leaving it manufactures an artefactual BLOCKED) · RE-BASE (its expected value conflicts with the change — NOT rewritten before the run: the change under test is normally an unmerged PR, so a pre-run rewrite makes the change its own oracle and the case can then only pass; it is carried into C1's --ids (NOT --also-ids, which /qa-regression declares mutually exclusive with --ids) and 5a rewrites it with the run's own evidence) · SUPERSEDED (the surface is gone — a proposal, never an edit; TRI-006 keeps retirement human). HARD RULE: every FILTERED_OUT row disposed RE-BASE appears in rebased_into_c1[], or its disposition is CONFIRMED/SUPERSEDED with a reason — an undisposed RE-BASE that never runs re-creates the exact gap this step closes. Step 2a files NO bug: a hit is a claim about a test case, never about the product. never_audited is context, not a verdict (TRI-000 reports WHEN a row was audited, never whether it is right). Spec: .claude/skills/qa-test/coverage-triage.md

scope.$comment: The tc:scope arguments actually used — recorded so the Step-3 verifier can re-run the identical scan, and so a later reader can tell a narrow triage from a thorough one. Scope comes from the manifest's own domain/tags/requiresModules vocabulary, never from diff paths; a path token may only ADD a suite, never filter one out.

counts.$comment: Straight from tc:scope --json. filtered_out is the coverage hole: a stale row that WILL run goes red at Step 4 and gets triaged, a stale row that will not run is invisible forever. not_executing (explicit Manual/Deprecated, EX-200/EX-201) is opted out by intent and is NOT a hole — kept as its own count so the number that measures real holes cannot lie.

repaired.$comment: Fixed BEFORE the run. Mechanics only — never an expected value.

rebased_into_c1.$comment: Carried in C1's --ids with its assertion UNCHANGED, so Step 4 can falsify it either way. Its Step-4 result and any 5a rewrite live in the normal triage record, not here.

superseded_proposals.$comment: Recorded, never edited — retirement is human (TRI-006) and tc:demote may only reach Manual.

unscannable.$comment: Reported, never read as an absence of risk. A legacy 11-column suite is REFUSED because parseSuite maps positionally, so its Priority is not Priority and runFate would be predicted off the wrong column.

test_data.$comment: The 2f test-data axis — the fifth derived pre-flight token (axes.md), and the only one that SUBTRACTS: it decides whether Step 3a dispatches test-data-engineer at all. Derived, never asked, never defaulted; "unresolved" treated as true. WHY IT EXISTS: 3a was an unconditional member of the Step-3 wave under a "seeded env, green td:validate" gate, with the only escape hatch one sentence in authoring.md phrased "skip ONLY when every planned case resolves" — default-on with a burden of proof to skip, so an opus agent was dispatched on runs whose cases resolved entirely against fixtures the environment already held. A false requires BOTH claims, not one: the planned @td()/{{VAR}} refs RESOLVE (deterministic, td:validate) AND no link under test needs a DIVERGENCE the fixtures lack (judgment, .claude/rules/test-data.md §SECOND RULE — Loyalty Missions resolved every alias and still left the mechanism question undecidable on flat $30 orders). fixtures_covering[] is mandatory when surface is false: an unstated skip reads exactly like a satisfied seed. It fails OPEN because authoring against data that cannot answer the question yields BLOCKED cases triaged as product defects, while a needless dispatch costs one browserless agent inside time the wave already spends. A NULL block means the axis never derived (a gap); surface:false WITH sources is the opposite.
surface_source: 1e-plan: 14 planned rows, all @td() refs already declared
value chain: no link needs a divergence beyond PROD_MOQ vs PROD_PACK
